The cohort skews young and pediatric-onset, with gastric primaries dominating the SDH-deficient strata.

outcome: objective response stratified by molecular subtype and drug

outcomes.name: ORR

Treatment-response data are retrospective (not from a prospective sub-trial) and the per-drug n's are small, but they remain the most-cited published anchor for sequencing TKIs in dSDH-GIST. Toxicity capture not feasible — paper is a registry/cohort analysis without per-AE tables.

intervention_dose: guadecitabine 45 mg/m^2 SC daily x 5 days, 28-day cycle
indication: SDH-deficient GIST, SDH-deficient PPGL, and HLRCC-associated RCC
population_detail: 9 patients enrolled before trial closed for low accrual (target 70); age 18-57, 6F/3M; 7 SDH-deficient GIST, 1 PPGL, 1 HLRCC-RCC. Trial used a Simon two-stage design (target ORR 30%, rule out 5%).
design: open-label, single-arm phase 2 (terminated for low accrual)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 0/9 objective responses across all three cohorts

safety_summary: Two patients developed treatment-limiting neutropenia; otherwise manageable toxicity. Hematologic AEs were the main signal.

toxicities.notes: Treatment-limiting in 2 of 9 — the dominant safety signal in this small cohort

intervention_dose: linsitinib 150 mg PO BID continuous, 28-day cycles
population_detail: 20 patients with WT-GIST enrolled in stage 1 of the SARC phase II trial. Rationale anchored on IGF1R overexpression observed preferentially in dSDH-GIST.
outcome: RECIST 1.1 ORR at 6 months; clinical benefit rate at 9 months
median_dor_or_pfs: mTTP 9.1 mo; PFS at 9 mo 52%; 9-mo clinical benefit rate 40%
safety_summary: Linsitinib was well tolerated. Drug-related grade 3+ events were uncommon at 1.8% of all reported drug-related events; the most frequent any-grade events were nausea (4.9% of events), fatigue (3.2%), abnormal liver function (3.2%), and diarrhea (2.5%).
notes: Hard negative on ORR. The 40% clinical-benefit rate at 9 months overlaps the natural-history indolence of dSDH-GIST, so it is not informative for drug activity. Closes IGF-1R inhibition as a strategy in this molecular subset. Reported AE rates are expressed as percent of drug-related events, not patient-level percentages — flagged in toxicities[] notes.

intervention_dose: olaparib 300 mg PO BID + temozolomide (dosing per case report; full details not in abstract)
indication: metastatic, multiply-relapsed SDH-deficient GIST + paraganglioma (single patient)
population_detail: Single pediatric/young-adult patient with SDHB-mutant GIST plus paraganglioma; multiply relapsed after prior TKI lines. Yale single-institution case report.

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: Case-level clinical response in multiply-relapsed dSDH-GIST + PGL

safety_summary: Case-report; per-AE detail not in the published letter.
notes: Letter-format case report with no abstract. The only published clinical evidence for PARP + alkylator in dSDH-GIST. Kept for the recurrence-contingency mechanism context — not enough signal to act on alone.

exclusion_reason: Trial enrolled localized primary KIT-positive GIST (CD117+) without molecular stratification; SDH-deficient GIST was not a recognized subtype in 2009 and the dSDH-GIST population was not represented in the cohort. The ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS guideline explicitly recommends avoiding adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST because imatinib has near-zero response in this molecular subset (Boikos 2016: 1/49 imatinib PR). The Z9001 1-year imatinib vs placebo result (RFS HR 0.35, 98% vs 83% at 1 yr; p<0.0001) does not transport to this patient.
notes: Captured for the audit trail as the foundational adjuvant-imatinib RCT (n=713). The board needs to see that the absence-of-evidence in dSDH-GIST is structural — these patients were never enrolled in the registration trials.

exclusion_reason: Same population mismatch as Z9001: SSGXVIII enrolled high-risk localized GIST by modified NIH consensus criteria with no SDH-status stratification, and the trial pre-dates the routine identification of SDH-deficient GIST. The 36-month vs 12-month finding (RFS HR 0.46; OS HR 0.45) is the basis of the 3-year adjuvant standard in KIT-mutant high-risk disease but does not transport to dSDH-GIST. ESMO-EURACAN-GENTURIS recommends against adjuvant imatinib in SDH-deficient GIST.
notes: n=397. Cited frequently in adjuvant-GIST discussions; the dossier needs the explicit exclusion call because the surgical team may ask 'why aren't we doing 3 years of adjuvant imatinib?' — answer: because the patient is in a subset that was not represented and that does not respond.

exclusion_reason: Same mechanism-scope rule — 10-year follow-up of the SSGXVIII trial population (KIT-mutant high-risk GIST, not SDH-deficient). 10-yr OS 79.0% (36-mo arm) vs 65.3% (12-mo arm); HR 0.55 (95% CI 0.37-0.83; p=0.004) reinforces the long-term benefit of extended adjuvant imatinib in the indications represented in the trial, but the dSDH-GIST subset is structurally absent.
notes: Long-term confirmation that the SSGXVIII benefit holds out to a decade — captured here so the audit trail shows the adjuvant-imatinib evidence was reviewed in full, not dismissed on the original 2012 paper alone.

exclusion_reason: Same scope rule: PERSIST-5 enrolled intermediate/high-risk primary GIST without SDH-status stratification. 5-year RFS 90% and OS 95%, but recurrences clustered in patients with imatinib-insensitive genotypes (PDGFRA D842V, KIT-WT) — and 49% of the cohort stopped treatment early. The PI3K/AKT-driven recurrence pattern after discontinuation reinforces that imatinib is suppressing imatinib-sensitive clones, not eradicating disease. dSDH-GIST is the canonical imatinib-insensitive subset.
notes: n=91. The PERSIST-5 design itself is the cleanest illustration of why adjuvant imatinib doesn't apply here: the trial separated out the imatinib-insensitive genotypes and showed they recur on or off treatment. dSDH-GIST belongs to the same insensitive class.

intervention_label: natural history and management of SDH-deficient GIST (narrative review)
population_detail: Narrative review covering dSDH-GIST natural history, surveillance, surgical recurrence patterns, and TKI-response data from the NIH wt-GIST clinic and published cohorts.
outcome: synthesis of dSDH-GIST recurrence rates, sites, and TKI activity by subtype
effect_size: median EFS ~2.5 yr post-resection in the NIH 76-patient surgical cohort; recurrence or progression in ~71% of dSDH-GIST patients
median_dor_or_pfs: median EFS 2.5 yr post-surgery (NIH 76-pt cohort cited)

outcomes.name: EFS
outcomes.notes: Citing the NIH retrospective surgical-management cohort (separate primary publication); 71% of patients had recurrence or progression

notes: The reference review the board will reach for to ground the surveillance question. Recurrence is the rule in dSDH-GIST even after R0 resection — drives the case for biennial whole-body MRI and PGL screening rather than adjuvant systemic therapy.

population_detail: 34 patients with KIT/PDGFRA-WT GIST without personal or family history of paraganglioma; tested for germline SDHB/C/D mutations.
design: prospective molecular cohort (Pediatric GIST Clinic, NIH/DFCI)
outcome: frequency of germline SDH defects in wt-GIST
effect_size: 4/34 (12%) WT-GIST patients carried germline SDH mutations

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: 4/34 sporadic WT-GIST had germline SDHB/C/D defects

notes: The paper that established SDH-deficient GIST as a real molecular entity beyond the Carney-Stratakis syndrome. Frames the diagnostic logic the board will use to interpret the SDHA L306P + Y408N + E350fs constellation in this case.

exclusion_reason: Cross-tumor extrapolation candidate but the PIK3CA R93W variant in this case sits outside the canonical alpelisib companion-diagnostic hotspots (E542K, E545K/A/D/G, H1047R/Y/L, C420R). SOLAR-1 enrolled HR+/HER2- breast cancer with the validated hotspot variants; the registration data (mPFS 11.0 vs 5.7 mo; HR 0.65, p<0.001) cannot be transported to a non-canonical PIK3CA variant in a histology where PI3K-pathway activation has no established driver role.
notes: n=572 (PIK3CA-mutant cohort). The dossier needs the explicit exclusion call because PIK3CA-mutant is one of the patient's user-stated targetable features. The right path forward is tissue confirmation of R93W and a sponsor-by-sponsor variant-eligibility check rather than borrowing the SOLAR-1 effect size.

exclusion_reason: Same scope rule as SOLAR-1 — INAVO120 enrolled HR+/HER2- breast cancer with canonical PIK3CA hotspot mutations (E542K, E545K, H1047R, etc.). PFS HR 0.43 (p<0.0001) and OS 34.0 vs 27.0 mo (HR 0.67, p=0.019) are registration-grade, but the R93W non-canonical variant in this case has not been shown to confer comparable inavolisib sensitivity, and breast-cancer histology adds a second mismatch layer.
notes: n=325. Captured for the audit trail so the board sees both PI3Kα-inhibitor pivotals were reviewed. The wt-GIST tersolisib trial (NCT05768139) the screener flagged is the right vehicle for any PI3Kα experiment, not the breast-cancer registration data.

indication: histiocytic sarcoma with MAP2K1 F53L activating mutation
population_detail: Single adult patient with metastatic histiocytic sarcoma, MAP2K1 F53L (negative regulatory domain), prior chemotherapy. MSKCC.
median_dor_or_pfs: durable response > 2 years on trametinib monotherapy

outcomes.name: CR_rate
outcomes.notes: Complete response by symptom resolution in 3 days; complete radiographic response durable >2 years

outcomes.name: DoR
outcomes.notes: Durable response ongoing at >2 years at time of report

safety_summary: Single-patient report; trametinib tolerated at standard 2 mg daily dose without dose modification reported.
notes: Cross-tumor precedent for MEK monotherapy in a MAP2K1-activating-mutation context, but F53L is in the negative-regulatory domain (class I MAP2K1 mutation) and this patient's P124S is at the αC-helix interface (class II behavior in melanoma data). Cross-tumor + cross-class — informs mechanism plausibility but does not transport effect size.

intervention_label: trametinib (in MAP2K1 K57N variant hairy cell leukemia)
exclusion_reason: Cross-tumor and cross-class. MAP2K1 K57N is a class I activating mutation in the negative-regulatory domain — biochemically distinct from the αC-helix P124 hotspot in this case. The hematologic-malignancy histology adds a second layer of mismatch. Single-patient hairy cell leukemia case with cutaneous response on trametinib does not transport to a wt-GIST patient.
notes: Reviewed to anchor whether any class-matched MEK-inhibitor data exists for the patient's P124S. They do not — the closest published precedents are class-I MAP2K1 mutations in non-GIST histologies.

intervention_label: MAP2K1 P124 hotspot characterization (resistance mechanism in BRAF-mutant melanoma on RAF/MEK combo)
indication: BRAF-mutant melanoma with acquired resistance to dabrafenib + trametinib
population_detail: Five melanoma patients with progression on combined RAF + MEK inhibition; tumor biopsies sequenced at progression.
design: molecular cohort — paired biopsies at baseline and progression
outcome: MAPK-pathway alterations at progression on RAF/MEK combination
effect_size: MEK2 Q60P identified as the dominant on-treatment resistance variant; MAP2K1 P124 mutations characterized as preexisting low-frequency alterations that diminish but do not eliminate BRAF-inhibitor response

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: Novel activating MEK2 mutation as primary resistance mechanism

notes: The reference paper for the framing of MAP2K1 P124 as a partial-resistance / partial-activating αC-helix variant. In melanoma, P124L/S/Q diminish dabrafenib response but tumors retain MEK-inhibitor sensitivity in vitro — the cleanest published mechanism rationale for considering trametinib in this patient's P124S, while flagging that the response data is melanoma-only and the variant alone has not anchored a positive-readout trial.

exclusion_reason: No published clinical readout for the wt-GIST cohort yet. LITESPARK-015 ASCO 2024/2025 data releases have covered the PPGL cohort (n=72, ORR 26%, DCR 85%, mPFS 22 mo) and the VHL/RCC cohorts, but the wt-GIST cohort has not reported. Trial-screener row already captures the protocol; no clinical-evidence row to write until the readout appears.
notes: Audited so the board knows the dossier reviewed the belzutifan wt-GIST evidence base and confirmed it is still pre-readout. Watch for ASCO 2026 / WCGIC for the GIST-cohort interim cut.

intervention_label: MGMT promoter methylation as TMZ-response biomarker in SDH-deficient GIST
population_detail: 65 GIST tumors profiled: 47 wt-GIST (33 SDH-deficient), 21 tyrosine-kinase-mutant. Single-institution Cambridge cohort.
design: retrospective molecular cohort with MGMT-methylation profiling
comparator: TKI-mutant GIST and SDH-preserved wt-GIST as comparators
outcome: frequency of MGMT promoter hypermethylation by GIST subtype
effect_size: MGMT hypermethylation in 8/33 (24%) SDH-deficient GIST; 0% in TKI-mutant or SDH-preserved wt-GIST

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: 8/33 SDH-deficient tumors had MGMT hypermethylation; 0/14 in SDH-preserved wt-GIST and 0/21 in TKI-mutant

notes: The published biomarker rationale for testing MGMT methylation if temozolomide enters the discussion at recurrence. The 24% MGMT-methylated subset is the patient population most likely to respond to TMZ in the dSDH-GIST setting. Aligns with the target_validation file's MGMT methylation row.

intervention_dose: sunitinib 50 mg PO daily, 4 wks on / 2 wks off (6-wk cycle)

population_detail: 312 patients (207 sunitinib, 105 placebo) with imatinib-resistant or -intolerant GIST. No SDH-status stratification; the cohort was overwhelmingly KIT-mutant by historical molecular epidemiology, with dSDH-GIST under-represented.
safety_summary: Most common treatment-related AEs were fatigue, diarrhea, skin discoloration, and nausea; G3+ rates not granularly extracted from abstract.

toxicities.notes: Most frequent treatment-related AE; G3+ rate not in abstract

notes: Pivotal RCT supporting sunitinib's FDA approval for 2L GIST. Captured as 'included' because (a) Boikos 2016 establishes sunitinib is the preferred 2L TKI in dSDH-GIST and (b) this is the registration-grade safety + efficacy anchor for the contingency plan at first recurrence. Detailed per-AE table beyond the abstract not retrieved here.

intervention_dose: regorafenib 160 mg PO daily x 3 wks every 4 wks
indication: advanced GIST after imatinib + sunitinib failure
population_detail: 199 patients (133 regorafenib, 66 placebo) with progression after both imatinib and sunitinib. No prospective SDH-status stratification; KIT-mutant disease dominated the population.
safety_summary: Characteristic regorafenib toxicities dominated G3 events: hypertension (23%), hand-foot skin reaction (20%), diarrhea (5%).

toxicities.notes: Most common G3 AE on regorafenib arm

notes: GRID pivotal — the registration-grade evidence base for the 3L TKI in the contingency plan. dSDH-GIST under-represented in the cohort; activity in this subset is by extrapolation plus the Dedousis 2025 review's qualitative claim of 'modest activity, similar to KIT-mutant 3L'.

indication: advanced GIST after >=3 prior TKIs (imatinib, sunitinib, regorafenib)
population_detail: 129 patients (85 ripretinib, 44 placebo) with >=3 prior TKIs. KIT-mutant disease dominated; prospective dSDH-GIST stratification not performed. 29 hospitals in 12 countries.
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 6.3 mo vs 1.0 mo; mOS 15.1 mo vs 6.6 mo

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: Median OS; hierarchical testing did not allow formal OS p-value because ORR was not significant

safety_summary: Ripretinib was better tolerated than other VEGFR-active TKIs in this setting; G3+ events were uncommon and headline rates included lipase increase 5%, hypertension 4%, fatigue 2%. Characteristic class effects (alopecia, hand-foot reaction) were any-grade in a majority but rarely G3+.

toxicities.notes: Most common G3+ AE on ripretinib arm
Common any-grade class effect; G3+ rare
Common any-grade; rarely G3+ on ripretinib

notes: INVICTUS pivotal for 4L+ GIST. The Mavroeidis 2025 review notes the dSDH-GIST evidence base for ripretinib is the weakest of the three post-imatinib TKIs — INVICTUS enrolled vanishingly few wt-GIST patients. Captured as 4L contingency anchor.

intervention_label: ICI in POLE proofreading-deficient hypermutators (rationale check)
exclusion_reason: Standard POLE → ICI rationale does not apply to this case. The published POLE-hypermutator → ICI-response literature (Rousseau 2021 J Clin Oncol; Domingo 2016; Bourdais 2017) is anchored on the canonical exonuclease/proofreading-domain hotspots P286R, V411L, S459F, S297F — variants that produce TMB ~100+ mut/Mb and ultramutated phenotypes. R1679 sits outside the exonuclease domain and the patient is TMB <1 mut/Mb and MSS. The variant is most plausibly a VUS with no ICI rationale; cancer-predisposition counseling is the right action.
notes: Captured to document that the dossier reviewed the POLE → ICI literature and the standard rationale does not transport. No separate per-paper rows for the POLE-hypermutator pembrolizumab data because the threshold question (canonical hotspot, TMB-high, MSI-H) is failed at the genotype level. Aligns with the validation file's POLE-counseling row.

intervention_dose: olverembatinib 40 mg PO every other day (RP2D; escalation range 20-50 mg QOD), continuous 28-day cycles
indication: advanced SDH-deficient GIST after prior TKI therapy
population_detail: 26 SDH-deficient GIST patients within a 66-patient phase 1b that also enrolled other solid tumors; median age 30 (range 13-56), 26.9% male, heavily pretreated with 65.4% having had at least two prior TKIs and 42.3% three.
design: open-label phase 1b dose-escalation plus biomarker-defined expansion cohort
safety_summary: All 66 patients had treatment-emergent AEs, mostly grade 1-2; grade 3 or higher treatment-related AEs occurred in 13.6% and no patient stopped for toxicity. The common events were leukocytosis, anemia, transaminase rise, hyperuricemia, and pyrexia.
notes: Largest prospective trial to date in this subtype and the signal behind the phase 3 NCT06640361. The safety table is reported across the full 66-patient phase 1b population rather than the 26-patient GIST cohort alone.

intervention_dose: vandetanib 300 mg PO daily in adults (100 mg/m^2 in patients under 18); reduced to 200 mg in two adults for toxicity
indication: SDH-deficient (KIT/PDGFRA wild-type) GIST in children and adults
population_detail: Nine patients (7 female, 2 male), median age 24 (range 11-52); all KIT/PDGFRA wild-type and SDH-deficient.

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 0/9; two patients had prolonged stable disease

safety_summary: Three of five adults started at 300 mg developed treatment-limiting toxicity (grade 3 hypertension, grade 2 seizure, grade 3 pneumonitis); the two children tolerated the drug without treatment-limiting events. No QT prolongation was seen.

toxicities.notes: Grade 3 hypertension, grade 2 seizure, grade 3 pneumonitis

notes: Negative phase 2 in exactly this molecular subtype: no objective responses across nine patients, with a 5.1-month median PFS and two prolonged stable diseases that plausibly reflect dSDH-GIST indolence rather than drug effect. Closes single-agent VEGFR/RET-directed TKI therapy as a strategy here. Grade-resolved safety from PMC6825553 Table 2; CT.gov NCT02015065 also posts an all-cause AE table.

intervention_dose: rogaratinib 800 mg PO twice daily, continuous 28-day cycles
indication: advanced SDH-deficient GIST (enrolled regardless of FGFR alteration status)
population_detail: 24 SDH-deficient GIST patients enrolled regardless of FGFR alteration status, on the rationale of FGFR/FGF upregulation in the subtype.
design: NCI multicenter open-label two-stage single-arm phase 2 (dSDH-GIST cohort)
safety_summary: Toxicities were manageable and dominated by the pan-FGFR class effects, chiefly hyperphosphatemia that tracked FGFR1 target engagement, plus fatigue and diarrhea. Per-term rates and grades are not in the abstract.

toxicities.notes: Characteristic pan-FGFR class effect tracking FGFR1 target engagement; rate not in abstract

notes: Positive readout and the highest objective response rate yet reported for any systemic agent in dSDH-GIST, well above imatinib's roughly 2%. Per-term safety rates were not retrievable: the abstract names only hyperphosphatemia, fatigue, and diarrhea, the CT.gov NCT04595747 results tab has no posted AE data, and the Nature Medicine full text is paywalled.

intervention_label: telaglenastat (CB-839, glutaminase inhibitor) in the SDH-deficient GIST cohort
exclusion_reason: The phase 1 basket (NCT02071862) carried a dedicated SDH-deficient GIST cohort, so the glutamine-dependence rationale fits the patient's biology, but no dSDH-GIST efficacy was ever published and Calithera wound the telaglenastat program down after its renal and lung studies missed. No primary-source effect size to extract.
notes: Documents that the glutaminase-metabolism route was tested in this subtype and is no longer an active program; the trial-screener row for NCT02071862 carries the registration detail.

exclusion_reason: ReDiscover's proof-of-concept enrolled canonical helical (E542K, E545K) and kinase (H1047R) PIK3CA hotspots in HR+/HER2- breast cancer; R93W was not studied and sits in the adaptor-binding domain outside the hotspots the mutant-selective allosteric design is built around. With the variant ctDNA-only and the histology different, the breast effect size does not transport, and a non-canonical, weaker-consequence variant predicts PI3K-alpha-inhibitor benefit less reliably than a hotspot call.
notes: The ReDiscover basket (NCT05216432) reads ctDNA and allows sponsor sign-off on non-canonical variants, so it is the most plausible enrollment route if tissue confirms R93W. Third PI3K-alpha row alongside alpelisib and inavolisib, all excluded on the same R93W grounds.

intervention_label: pemigatinib (FGFR1-3 inhibitor) in the SDH-deficient GIST cohort
exclusion_reason: The dedicated dSDH-GIST trial (NCT07434843, George/DFCI) opened in 2026 with no clinical readout yet, so there is no primary-source efficacy or safety to compile. The FGFR-pathway rationale it tests is now anchored by the positive rogaratinib phase 2 (Merriam 2026).
notes: 24-patient single-arm trial to watch for a first readout; until then the rogaratinib row carries the FGFR-pathway evidence base for this subtype.
